composio.note: Composio lists Outlook under 'Composio-managed OAuth available'. Bring your own app registration for your own name and verified badge on the consent prompt, extra Graph permissions, or to let customer tenant admins grant consent to an app they recognise. Composio's Outlook guide suggests 'Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts' and Mail.Read, Mail.Send, offline_access plus openid profile email. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio auth-config screen.

summary: Registering the app is fast and free, and there is no Microsoft app review for Graph mail permissions. The real friction is in customer tenants: unverified multitenant apps show an unverified-publisher warning, many tenants restrict user consent to verified publishers or disable it, and then an admin must consent. Publisher verification removes most of that but requires a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account.
difficultyReason: Registration is self-serve in minutes. Publisher verification needs a Partner Center (CPP) account with completed business verification, a DNS-verified domain matching the publisher domain, and specific admin roles, which is paperwork rather than review. Tenant consent policies are outside your control.

time.notes: Hands-on: 20-40 min to register, add redirect URI, permissions and secret (inferred); 1-2 hours more for publisher verification if CPP prerequisites exist (inferred). Approval: None for registration. Publisher verification takes minutes once CPP prerequisites are met (source); CPP account verification itself can take days (inferred). To production: Same day for personal accounts and permissive tenants; days to weeks (inferred) for enterprise tenants that require publisher verification or admin consent.

review.details: No Microsoft review of the app or its Graph permissions. Publisher verification is self-serve: link a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program Partner One ID (the partner global account, not a location ID) to the app registration. It is free and needs no license. Separate optional programs (Microsoft 365 Publisher Attestation, App Certification) exist but are not required for OAuth.

limitsBeforeApproval: Unverified multitenant apps registered after Nov 8, 2020 that request more than basic sign-in and profile cannot get user consent in other tenants where risk-based step-up consent is enabled; users see an unverified-publisher warning. Tenants using the 'verified publishers, selected permissions' policy also block user consent, routing users to an admin or the admin consent workflow. Personal Microsoft accounts are unaffected.

prerequisites.item: Microsoft Entra tenant and an account with at least Application Developer role
prerequisites.why: Required to create app registrations. A free Azure account works.

prerequisites.item: Work or school (Entra) account, not a personal Microsoft account, as registrant
prerequisites.why: Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account cannot be publisher verified.

prerequisites.item: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account (partner global account) that has passed verification
prerequisites.why: Required for publisher verification and the blue verified badge.

prerequisites.item: DNS-verified custom domain set as the app's publisher domain (not *.onmicrosoft.com)
prerequisites.why: Must match the domain of the email used in CPP verification.

prerequisites.item: Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in Entra, plus CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin in Partner Center, signed in with MFA
prerequisites.why: The person who initiates publisher verification needs both role sets.

steps.title: Choose supported account types
steps.detail: For a multi-customer agent pick 'Multiple Entra ID tenants', or 'Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts' to include Outlook.com users (Composio's guide uses the latter). Note this choice changes redirect URI rules (no query params, no wildcards, max 100 URIs with personal accounts).

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Entra admin center > Entra ID > App registrations > New registration. Enter name and account type, register, and record the Application (client) ID.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Authentication > Add a platform > Web. Paste the redirect URI copied from the Composio auth-config screen.

steps.title: Add delegated Microsoft Graph permissions
steps.detail: API permissions > Add > Microsoft Graph > Delegated: offline_access, openid, profile, email, User.Read, and the narrowest mail permissions needed (Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send). Avoid application permissions unless you need daemon access; those always require admin consent.

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.detail: Certificates & secrets > New client secret. Maximum lifetime is 24 months; Microsoft recommends under 12. Copy the value immediately; it is never shown again. Set a reminder to rotate it in Composio before expiry.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Composio dashboard > Create Auth Config > Outlook > OAuth2 > own credentials. Paste client ID, secret, scopes; confirm redirect URI matches exactly.

steps.title: Test with a personal account and a second tenant
steps.detail: Connect one personal Microsoft account and one work account from another tenant to see the real consent prompt and any unverified-publisher warning.

steps.title: Set publisher domain and check publisher-verification readiness
steps.detail: Verify the custom domain in the tenant, set it as publisher domain, and confirm the CPP account, roles and email domain line up.

steps.title: Enroll in Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program
steps.detail: Create the Partner Center account and complete business verification if you do not have one. Legal attestations and company details are yours to provide.

steps.title: Mark the app as publisher verified
steps.detail: App registration > Branding & properties > add the Partner One ID and verify. Done in minutes when prerequisites are met.

steps.title: Prepare admin-consent instructions for customers
steps.detail: Draft a short note for customer IT with the admin consent URL (https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/adminconsent?client_id=...), the permission list and why each is needed.

nuances.title: Unverified publisher warning
nuances.detail: Multitenant apps without publisher verification show a warning, and with risk-based step-up consent enabled users in other tenants cannot consent at all.

nuances.title: Customer tenant consent policy decides
nuances.detail: Tenants can allow user consent for any app, only for verified publishers with low-impact permissions, or disable it. In the restrictive cases an admin must consent or approve via the admin consent workflow.

nuances.title: Client secret expires
nuances.detail: Secrets last at most 24 months. When one expires every Composio connection using it fails until you rotate the secret in the auth config.

nuances.title: Personal accounts tighten redirect rules
nuances.detail: Including personal Microsoft accounts disallows query parameters and wildcards and caps redirect URIs at 100 (256 for org-only).

nuances.title: Publisher verification is free
nuances.detail: No charge and no license; the cost is CPP enrollment effort.

nuances.title: Apps that require user assignment
nuances.detail: If a customer sets the enterprise app to require assignment, an admin must consent even when user consent is otherwise allowed.

blockers.problem: Users in customer tenants cannot consent ('Need admin approval')
blockers.whatToDo: Complete publisher verification and give the customer admin the admin consent URL, or ask them to enable the admin consent workflow.

blockers.problem: Publisher verification fails on domain mismatch
blockers.whatToDo: Make the CPP verification email domain match the app's publisher domain or a DNS-verified domain in the tenant; *.onmicrosoft.com is not accepted.

blockers.problem: App registered with a personal Microsoft account
blockers.whatToDo: Re-register under an Entra work or school tenant associated with the CPP partner global account.
Copy the redirect URI from Composio exactly, including case and path; add it to the Web platform on the application object.

agentCanDo: Recommend account type and the minimal delegated Graph permissions for the agent's mail features
Generate the admin consent URL and a customer-IT explainer
Check publisher-verification prerequisites (domain match, roles, PGA vs location ID)
Verify the redirect URI matches Composio's value and Entra's rules
Track secret expiry and remind before rotation
With Graph API access, script the app registration and permission setup
developerMustDo: Own the Entra tenant and sign in with MFA
Create the app registration and client secret, and paste the secret into Composio
Verify the custom domain via DNS
Enroll and verify the business in Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program and accept the identity platform Terms of Use
Ask customer tenant admins to grant consent where required
redirectUri: Must start with https, except localhost (http allowed; port ignored for matching). Case-sensitive path match; URIs without a path get a trailing slash in responses. Max 256 characters each; max 256 URIs for org-only apps, 100 when personal accounts are included. Wildcards only for org-only apps via the manifest, and discouraged. Query parameters not allowed when personal accounts are supported. No IPv6 loopback, no IDNs, no ! $ ' ( ) , ; characters.

claims.claim: Publisher verification requires a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program partner global account; location Partner One IDs are not supported.
Publisher verification is free, needs no license, and completes in minutes once prerequisites are met.
Since November 2020, with risk-based step-up consent enabled, users cannot consent to unverified multitenant apps requesting more than basic sign-in and profile.
Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account cannot be publisher verified, and *.onmicrosoft.com cannot be the publisher domain.
Built-in consent policy microsoft-user-default-low allows user consent only for verified publishers or same-tenant apps and only for low-impact permissions.
Redirect URIs must be https except localhost; localhost port is ignored for matching; wildcards unsupported when personal accounts are included.
Client secrets are limited to 24 months; Microsoft recommends under 12 months.
Delegated Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send, User.Read and offline_access do not require admin consent by default.
Composio offers a managed Outlook OAuth app.
Enterprise tenants with restricted consent can add days to weeks before users can connect.

openQuestions: Composio docs show differing redirect URIs (composio.dev/auth/outlook: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback; other pages: .../api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback or .../api/v1/auth-apps/add). Copy from the dashboard.
Admin-consent requirement for Mail.* delegated permissions was not confirmed from the fetched page section (permissions reference too long to read fully); confirm per permission.
How long Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program business verification takes is not published on the pages fetched.
What share of enterprise tenants enable restrictive consent policies is unknown.
